worked_solution:
If $F=P\,i+Q\,j$ is a vector field and $C$ is a piecewise-smooth, simple, closed curve, then the flux of $F$ across $C$ is given by

$$
{∮}_{C}F\cdot n\,\text{d}s={∮}_{C}P\,\text{d}y-Q\,\text{d}x,
$$

where $n$ denotes the outward-pointing unit normal vector to $C.$ 

Along the curve $C,$ we have

$$
x=7\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,y=2\operatorname{sin}⁡t.
$$

 

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}P(x,y) & ={x}^{2}=49{cos}^{2}⁡t, \\ Q(x,y) & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing the derivatives of $x(t)$ and $y(t)$ along the curve, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(7\operatorname{cos}⁡t)=-7\operatorname{sin}⁡t, \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2\operatorname{sin}⁡t)=2\operatorname{cos}⁡t.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate the integral using the substitution $\operatorname{sin}⁡t=u,du=\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,dt,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∮}_{C}F\cdot n\,\text{d}s & ={∮}_{C}P\,\text{d}y-Q\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }(P\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}-Q\cdot \frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t})\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }(49{cos}^{2}⁡t)\cdot (2\operatorname{cos}⁡t)-(1)\cdot (-7\operatorname{sin}⁡t)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }98{cos}^{3}⁡t+7\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }98{cos}^{2}⁡t\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡t+7\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }98(1-{sin}^{2}⁡t)\operatorname{cos}⁡t+7\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }98(\operatorname{cos}⁡t-{sin}^{2}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t)+7\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }98\operatorname{cos}⁡t+7\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,\text{d}t+{\int }_{0}^{2\pi }-98{sin}^{2}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,dt \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }98\operatorname{cos}⁡t+7\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,\text{d}t+{\int }_{0}^{0}-98{u}^{2}\,du \\  & =(98\operatorname{sin}⁡t-7\operatorname{cos}⁡t){|}_{0}^{2\pi }+0 \\  & =0\end{aligned}
$$

If F=Pi+Qj is a vector field and C is a piecewise-smooth, simple, closed curve, then the flux of F across C is given by ∮CF⋅nds=∮CPdy−Qdx, where n denotes the outward-pointing unit normal vector to C.

Along the curve C, we have x=7cos⁡t,y=2sin⁡t.

Therefore,

P(x,y)=x2=49cos2⁡t,Q(x,y)=1.

Computing the derivatives of x(t) and y(t) along the curve, we get

dxdt=ddt(7cos⁡t)=−7sin⁡t,dydt=ddt(2sin⁡t)=2cos⁡t.

Finally, we evaluate the integral using the substitution sin⁡t=u,du=cos⁡tdt, as follows:

∮CF⋅nds=∮CPdy−Qdx=∫02π(P⋅dydt−Q⋅dxdt)dt=∫02π(49cos2⁡t)⋅(2cos⁡t)−(1)⋅(−7sin⁡t)dt=∫02π98cos3⁡t+7sin⁡tdt=∫02π98cos2⁡t⋅cos⁡t+7sin⁡tdt=∫02π98(1−sin2⁡t)cos⁡t+7sin⁡tdt=∫02π98(cos⁡t−sin2⁡tcos⁡t)+7sin⁡tdt=∫02π98cos⁡t+7sin⁡tdt+∫02π−98sin2⁡tcos⁡tdt=∫02π98cos⁡t+7sin⁡tdt+∫00−98u2du=(98sin⁡t−7cos⁡t)|02π+0=0
